subject: Acme - intermittent 5xx/429 spikes; replayed retries blamed on auth header misclassification
messages:
From: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acmecorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Platform SRE <sre@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spikes in 5xx/429 during morning traffic window (possible token validation issue)

Hi Aditya and Lauren,

We're seeing repeated spikes in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood API across our ingestion pipeline between 08:40-09:10 PT. This is accompanied by dramatic client-side retry amplification — requests that should resolve in <200ms are timing out and the retry pattern is causing a thundering wave that impacts throughput.

Key facts:
- Window: ~08:40-09:10 PT today (Apr 18)
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx and 429, timeouts, many repeated identical requests in a short window
- Recent changes: we rotated tokens on our side at 07:50 PT and patched some clocks on a subset of hosts.

SRE suspects some auth validation bounce (we're seeing JWTs rejected then accepted intermittently from our edge logs) and that Redwood's gateway may be classifying certain token failures as 5xx instead of 401/403. This is triggering our client-side exponential backoff to misfire and replay identical requests rapidly.

Can you confirm whether there was any change to token validation, gateway rate-limiting, or a known clock skew issue on your side? This is causing significant ingestion lag on our side. We're happy to join a call now.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Baker
Platform Engineering, Acme Corp


From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acmecorp.com>

I'll follow up with an update within 20 minutes. We can also divert traffic to an alternate pool if we confirm misclassification is driving retries.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spikes in 5xx/429 during morning traffic window (possible token validation issue)

Tom / Aditya — quick technical readout from the edge and token svc while I was triaging on the bridge earlier:

Findings so far:
- We see a pattern where incoming requests with slightly skewed iat/exp (clock differences of ~30-90s) are hitting our auth validation hot path. Instead of returning a clear 401/invalid-token, an internal fallback path to the token-introspection service returns a 500 when introspection times out.
- The gateway translates that 500 into a 5xx for the client. Our rate-limiter also interprets bursts of these errors and responds with 429s in some backend pools.
- The combination: transient token validation timeouts -> 500s -> client retries -> amplified load -> downstream 429 and legit 5xx due to overloaded pools.

I've attached a trimmed log (auth-debug.log) and a representative request trace (request-trace-0418.json) showing headers, the JWT iat/exp, the internal traceback and the 500 returned from the introspection service.

Mitigations we've applied mid-incident:
- Adjusted gateway mapping so token-introspection timeouts map to 401 instead of 500 for the next 30 minutes (temporary rule).
- Increased introspection service timeouts on the pool handling Acme traffic by +250ms to reduce false timeouts.
- Temporarily exempted Acme from automatic rate-limit escalation to stop 429 overlay while we stabilize.

Next steps (action items):
- Patch: change fallback to return 401 on invalid/skewed tokens (INFRA-3142) — target: patch by 2027-04-19 18:00 PT.
- Postmortem: full RCA and client guidance on clock skew tolerances.
- Post-fix: run a controlled replay with your SREs to validate.

Notes: you mentioned token rotation earlier — if new tokens were issued with shorter exp leeway that can magnify the effect. If you can confirm the rotation window (UTC timestamps) that'd help.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: auth-debug.log (trimmed)
Attachment: request-trace-0418.json (redacted)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Escalation: Acme ingestion impact — executive attention requested

Team — following Dev's triage, this is escalating beyond a standard SRE action. Acme is reporting production ingestion delays across multiple teams and the issue is visible in their dashboards (they've CC'd Platform SRE).

Suggested exec asks:
- Immediate: confirm temporary routing and mapping changes remain in place until patch is deployed.
- Credits: offer a small goodwill credit for the window (Aditya, propose amount and we'll route to finance).
- Communications: prepare a short customer-facing summary and an internal incident timeline.
- Leadership: loop in Rishi for potential SLA exceptions if the patch window slips.

Please confirm ownership for the commit and ETA. Prioritize both the patch (INFRA-3142) and a follow-up remediation plan that prevents misclassification of auth errors.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference


From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-19T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme - mitigation summary and next steps (INFRA-3142)

Tom — summary and next steps from Redwood: thanks again for the quick coordination.

What we changed (completed 2027-04-18):
- Temporary gateway rule to map token-introspection timeouts -> 401 (reverted to default behavior for other tenants at 04:30 PT).
- Increased introspection svc timeouts + temporary rate-limit exemption for Acme traffic.
- Monitored for 24 hours; error rate returned to baseline by 11:00 PT and steady through today.

Planned fix (target):
- INFRA-3142: patch fallback to explicitly return 401 for invalid/skewed tokens and improve logging for token-introspection failures. Target deploy: 2027-04-19 20:00 PT.
- Postmortem and customer write-up: draft by 2027-04-20 14:00 PT, will include guidance for clock skew tolerance and token rotation best practices.

Credits/Comp: Aditya will propose a goodwill credit and we will escalate to finance after sign-off.

Follow-ups / links:
- PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-8927
